sections.h2: What the Halifax County recording office does
sections.html:
The office takes in, indexes and safeguards land records. It also handles plats, UCC filings, vital records and assorted miscellaneous documents. The elected register serves a 4-year term and leads a team of one assistant and four deputies.

Business runs from half past eight to five on weekdays, holidays excepted. An online Register of Deeds Index Search is linked from the county site. The county budget for 2026-27 sets aside $516,743 for the office.

sections.h2: How far back the records go
sections.html:
Paper indexes reach to 1732, which is older than the county itself. Online, the index search offers three layers:

  • Indexes and images of recorded real property documents from 1976 forward.
  • Historical real estate indexes for 1934 through 1975.
  • Survey maps dating from 1818.

Other record sets start at different points. Marriage records begin in 1825, and birth and death records begin in October 1913. Anything on a parcel that predates 1976 means working from the historical or hard-copy indexes.

Under a commissioners' rule that took effect January 1, 2016, the register will not accept a deed conveying real property unless the Tax Collector certifies that no delinquent ad valorem tax, or other tax the collector must collect, encumbers the parcel.

Staff need time to research each parcel, so the collector stops taking deeds at 4:30 in the afternoon. The collector's office is Tax Administration, 357 Ferrell Lane in Halifax, phone 252-583-2121. Do this step before you go to the register, since a deed without the certification is turned away. Bring the deed itself, the parcel description and a phone number where the collector can reach your attorney if a question comes up. Our Halifax County property tax guide covers rates, appeals and relief.

The 2026-27 fee schedule lists $26 for an instrument up to 15 pages and $64 for a deed of trust or mortgage up to 35 pages, adding $4 for each page past those limits. State law fixes the same base amounts.

The schedule also lists $10 for each added index reference on an assignment, $2 per party past 20 distinct parties, and 25 cents a page for photocopies and scanned images. State law treats its fee list as complete and exclusive, collected at filing.

Halifax lists the excise stamp tax at $1.00 per $500 of consideration, with any remainder counted as another $500. State law matches that figure and places the duty on the party giving up title, who must pay before the deed is recorded.

Revenue is split in two. The county general fund keeps one portion, and the state revenue department receives the rest monthly after refunds and an allowance. The 2026-27 county budget shows $353,500 for the Register of Deeds among other taxes and licenses. A parcel split across county lines pays in the county holding the larger share. Ask your closing attorney for the exact amount before settlement.

sections.h2: Recording rules for contracts for deed
sections.html:
Registration is what gives a deed, option or long lease its force against lien creditors and later paying purchasers, and the order of registration sets priority among competing claims.

Seller financing falls under Chapter 47H when the buyer will make at least five payments besides the down payment, the seller keeps title, and the property is a principal dwelling of one to four families or a manufactured home with a price of $5,000 or more. Three features stand out:

  • The agreement must be written, signed and acknowledged.
  • The seller records it, or a Memorandum of a Contract for Deed, within five business days.
  • The buyer may cancel through midnight of the third business day, and a default notice must allow a cure date at least 30 days out.

Ask an attorney to draft any land contract and to confirm that it was recorded.

Beyond deeds, the 2026-27 fee schedule prices the vital records and notary services that run through the same counter:

  • Marriage license: $60, which includes the $35 state fee.
  • Certified copy of a birth certificate or a death certificate: $10 each.
  • Notary public oath administered: $10, and $5 to verify a commission.
  • Military service record: no charge.

The same schedule prices a certified plat copy at $5 for the first page and lists right-of-way plans at $21 for the first page and $5 for each added page.

sections.h2: Tax foreclosure sales and the land records
sections.html:
A tax foreclosure auction ends with a deed, which the register records. The county publishes each sale notice on its Tax Foreclosures page, and bidding happens in the courthouse lobby at Halifax. A bid stays open to a higher one for 10 days, and the property goes as is.

Buyers take subject to taxes, assessments and liens held by parties who were not named defendants, so a title examination before bidding is wise. If your own house faces a tax sale, selling before the auction keeps the price in your hands, and the register will record your deed once the tax certification is on file.

The county has 25,078 homes and apartments and 20,383 households. Owners hold 62.9% of occupied homes, a middle-priced owned home is valued at $106,200, and rent sits at a median of $813. Seniors make up 25.2% of the population. Only 75 permits for new building were issued in 2025.

A practical order for a seller: pay or confirm the tax balance, get the collector's certification, gather payoff letters and confirm old loans have recorded satisfactions, then have your attorney finalize the deed. The excise stamp tax is paid at recording. A cash sale skips a lender's paperwork, but the certification and the stamp tax stay. Allow extra days if a municipal balance shows on the parcel, because the collector has to research it before the deed can be accepted. Keep copies of the certification and the recorded deed with your closing papers.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Halifax County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Weekdays from half past eight to five, with holidays closed. The tax certification a deed needs is handled at the Tax Collector's office, which closes its deed window a half hour before the register's counter.

faqs.q: How much will a Halifax County filing run?
faqs.a: The 2026-27 schedule shows $26 for up to 15 pages plus $4 for every added page, and $25 more for a non-standard form. The seller also owes the excise stamp tax of $1.00 per $500 of value.

faqs.q: What can make the Halifax County register reject a deed?
faqs.a: A missing certification from the Tax Collector is one reason. A county rule effective January 1, 2016 bars the register from accepting a deed until delinquent taxes are cleared and certified, so visit Tax Administration first.

faqs.q: How old are the land records the Halifax County register holds?
faqs.a: Paper indexes go back to 1732. Online search covers recorded documents from 1976 forward, historical indexes for 1934 through 1975, and survey maps from 1818.

faqs.q: Is recording a satisfaction of a mortgage free in Halifax County?
faqs.a: Yes. The fee schedule shows no charge for satisfactions, consistent with state law. A deed of trust itself starts at $64 for its first 35 pages.
